record.original_question: Is the single-machine scheduling problem 1||sum w_j T_j, which minimizes total weighted tardiness, fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time of any job?

If each job j ∈ J has a due date dj ∈ N, we also minimize – the total weighted tardiness P j∈J wjT j, where T j = max{0, dj − Cj}, and – the weighted number of tardy jobs, P j∈J wjUj.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the single-machine scheduling problem defined as follows. We are given a set J = {1, 2, ..., n} of jobs to be processed non-preemptively on a single machine that can process at most one job at a time. Each job j ∈ J has:
- a positive integer processing time p_j ∈ ℕ,
- a positive integer weight w_j ∈ ℕ, and
- a due date d_j ∈ ℕ.

A schedule is a permutation of J specifying the order in which the jobs are processed starting at time 0; under such a schedule, the completion time C_j of job j is the sum of the processing times of all jobs scheduled up to and including j. The tardiness of job j is T_j = max{0, C_j − d_j}. The objective is to find a schedule minimizing the total weighted tardiness
   Σ_{j ∈ J} w_j · T_j.

Let p_max = max_{j ∈ J} p_j denote the maximum processing time of any job. 

Question: Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max? That is, does there exist a computable function f and a constant c such that the problem can be solved in time f(p_max) · n^c, where n = |J| is the number of jobs?
artifact.status_search_result: No publication was found that resolves the fixed-parameter tractability status of 1||Σw_jT_j parameterized by p_max. The problem was posed as an open problem in a 2017 survey on parameterized complexity of scheduling, and recent work on parameterized scheduling (e.g., on rejection, low-rank processing-time matrices, late-work criteria) does not appear to settle it. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Scheduling Meets Fixed-Parameter Tractability
status_evidence.snippet: Parameterized complexity analysis of NP-hard single-machine scheduling problems with respect to parameters including p_max.
status_evidence.claim: The FPT status of weighted tardiness minimization parameterized by p_max is treated within the parameterized scheduling literature as an open question.

status_evidence.title: A new perspective on single-machine scheduling problems with late work related criteria
status_evidence.snippet: Parameterized complexity analysis of NP-hard single-machine problems with respect to number of different processing times, number of different due dates, p_max, and d_max.
status_evidence.claim: Recent parameterized analyses focus on related (late-work) criteria and on different parameters; they do not resolve FPT status of 1||Σw_jT_j by p_max.
